newsitem.title: JAPAN: Chirac happy to cast himself as salesman in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Chirac happy to cast himself as salesman in Japan.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac, on the last day of official business in Japan, told compatriots he had no qualms about swapping the role of statesman for that of a salesman of French products.
"I have no qualms about that," Chirac told French expatriates at a business breakfast on Wednesday when asked whether he had the impression he was playing the role of trade minister.
For too long, French leaders had considered the diplomatic profession and geopolitics "noble" and matters of economic or logistical importance "less noble", Chirac said.
"A head of state or prime minister has to defend all the interests of the state wherever he goes, including its economic interests."

On a previous official visit to Japan when he was Prime Minister under President Francois Mitterrand in the late 1980s, Chirac was ridiculed by the French media for seeming too much of a car salesman.
One French business leader voiced cautious approval of Chirac's current double role.

"The German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, American President Bill Clinton clearly represent their commercial interests. The latter rarely hesitates to pick up the phone to ask any a country to buy U.S. planes. France has moved in that direction, but it isn't altogether there yet," said Lionel Requillart, vice-president of Pierre Fabre Japon, a cosmetics and pharmaceuticals firm.

"Businesses must take matters in to their hands and not expect spectacular results from state visits like this one," said Requillart, "But we do ask the government to create a favourable environment for product sales and investments."
Other heads of enterprises at the breakfast were also concerned that France had not yet done enough, especially in Japan's insurance markets.

"The weak presence of foreigners in the life-insurance markets is due to strict regulations on the product and the control of their prices by ministries," said James Hawken, president of insurance company Axa Japon.

During his visit to Japan, which began on Sunday, Chirac has also appeared to criticise his predecessors for ignoring too long a country which has rocketed to second place on the global economic scale. He noted that he was only the second French president to visit Japan since World War Two.

Chirac was to meet Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Wednesday evening for a private dinner. On Monday the two signed an agreement entitled "20 Points For The Year 2000", designed to take Franco-Japanese relations on to a higher plane.
On Thursday, Chirac is due to make a private visit to Japan's southern island of Kyushu where a sumo wrestling tournament is currently being held. He is scheduled to return to Paris on Friday.
